explanation: The clause 'its modal owner window' rests on no cited line: add Main.vb 758 (DownloadAdmx.ShowDialog) as evidence. Also 'until the process is killed' is loose: killing a hung msiexec makes WaitForExit return, the exit code is non-zero and the catch at 123-127 re-enables the dialog; only a stalled DownloadFile (no child to kill) or the whole application needs the process ended. Say which stall each remedy ends.

'an earlier failed run, which is never cleaned up' is false: line 114 deletes the whole scratch folder, but only after the moves at 103-111, so leftovers are removed by the next successful run, after they were in the unpack target. Rewrite: the folder is cleaned only when a run succeeds. Also state the reach the lines show: stale files in the unpack folder sit under the paths the move reads (103-111), so a leftover top-level file or language folder of an older package that the new unpack does not overwrite is moved into the destination. Further, 'the system's search order decides which executable runs' rests on knowledge of how Process.Start resolves a bare name (UseShellExecute defaults true), which is outside the code: add externalSource, or reduce the claim to 'started as msiexec with no path (line 90)'. The record merges two harms (search order, leftovers) under one risk; give each its own finding with its own category.
